id: Simon Torring::3m::Southeast Asia e-commerce is growing "too fast" at the moment - what's going on? It's really hard to forecast in e-comme
author: Simon Torring
headline: Co-Founder at Cube
text: Southeast Asia e-commerce is growing "too fast" at the moment - what's going on? It's really hard to forecast in e-commerce, but at Cube we have to try. One of our long-held beliefs is that 2012-2021 was about sales growth from new users shopping online, and that 2022-2031 will be predominantly about existing online shoppers moving more of their total spending from offline channels to online ones year by year. That logic gives us expected annual online market growth of something like 15% here and now. But e-commerce is growing much faster than that, and has even sped up in recent quarters. What's going on? In short, we believe the offline-to-online shift is happening faster than we had predicted, because online shopping is getting better faster. We've seen something like this once before, when TikTok Shop started generating serious sales in 2023-2024: Rather than cannibalizing Shopee and Lazada, it mostly generated new purchase occasions that were pulling dollars from offline to online. Now it seems to be happening again, and we hypothesize that the following drivers are making it happen: 1) E-commerce delivery quality is improving very quickly, especially same-day and QuickCommerce (<4 hours). Shopee is by far the most important actor for this trend. It's simply making e-commerce a bit more convenient than going to the mall for a lot of purchases. 2) Creator and live commerce are deepening, especially driven by commission/affiliate economics. Large brands are moving more of their marketing budgets into these channels, which is leading to more and better content, which is leading to more sales - especially content commerce. 3) Generative AI is being used by more than half of the region's online shoppers now, across the product discovery and/or selection steps. That is also pulling purchase occasions online that were previously fulfilled through offline retail. There's also others, like consumer credit (Shopee's buy now pay later offering is more generous than what most consumers can get offline...). Note: We believe Shopee, Lazada, and TikTok Shop as a group are growing faster than overall e-commerce, so while they are up +32% yoy, total e-com is probably more like 21-22%. Fascinating times... … more
